title: How to Clean Kitchen Cabinets

seo.title: How to Clean Kitchen Cabinets
seo.meta_description: Clean kitchen cabinets by removing dust and grease with minimal moisture and a cleaner compatible with paint, wood, veneer, or laminate. Dry edges and seams.
seo.search_intent: Clean cabinet doors and fronts without damaging paint, veneer, wood, laminate, or hardware while removing cooking grease.

excerpt: Kitchen grease bonds with dust into a sticky film that makes strong cleaner tempting. Identify the finish first because painted wood, veneer, laminate, and sealed wood have different limits.
content_html:
Start in an inconspicuous spot. The cabinet finish matters more than how stubborn the grease looks. A degreaser that is fine on laminate may dull paint or clear finish.

Remove dust before degreasing

Wipe doors, trim, and cabinet tops with a dry microfiber cloth. That keeps hard particles from being dragged around when moisture is added.

Use minimal liquid and start mild

Warm water with a small amount of mild detergent handles a lot of fresh soil. Dampen the cloth rather than soaking the door and work in manageable sections.

Grease near the range may need more contact time, not more force

Let a finish-compatible cleaner work for the labeled time and repeat if necessary. Avoid abrasive pads and strong solvents unless the cabinet maker permits them.

Dry edges, seams, and hardware

Moisture entering engineered wood, veneer edges, or joints can cause swelling. Pay particular attention around handles where hand oils and cooking grease combine.

If the cloth picks up cabinet color, stop

You may be removing paint or stain rather than dirt. Switch to a milder method and follow manufacturer care instructions when available.

A quick weekly wipe around cooking areas and handles prevents grease from aging into a much harder sticky film.

faq.question: Can I use a strong degreaser?
faq.answer: Only if it is compatible with the cabinet finish. Test a hidden area first.

faq.question: Why do cabinet edges swell?
faq.answer: Engineered wood and veneer edges can absorb moisture through seams; use little liquid and dry promptly.

faq.question: What if the cloth picks up color?
faq.answer: You may be removing paint or stain. Stop and switch to a gentler method.
